item.title: Google just told schools: turn off our AI and you lose Google Search
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Starting in early 2027, Gemini, NotebookLM and Google Search will be switched off for school-managed K-12 student accounts. Administrators must turn them on. It reverses Google's August move to switch Gemini on by default in Classroom. Schools cannot keep classic Search and drop only the AI Overviews. Block AI entirely, and students lose Google Search too. "Search and AI are deeply integrated," said Google's education chief Chris Phillips. Sources: Chalkbeat, Forbes, CNN (via ABC17 News), Techaeris.

item.title: Y Combinator's CEO spends up to $200,000 a year on AI tokens. His agents even read his therapy notes
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On Walter Isaacson's podcast The Builders, Garry Tan estimated he spends roughly $100,000 to $200,000 a year on tokens. He uses AI agents for coding and countless work projects. Tan says his agent reads his email, Dropbox, Apple Notes and "even my therapy notes going back 20 years." He also had an agent research Isaacson's podcast to prepare for the interview. Y Combinator runs an internal agent called Stray Light with context on every founder it backed and every application. Sources: TechCrunch, NewsBytes, Superpower Daily.

item.title: Anthropic just admitted in its IPO filing that self-building AI may be imminent
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic's revised IPO filing, made on November 2, says its internal estimates show it "may imminently meet" a key safety threshold. That threshold is AI that dramatically speeds up AI progress, known as recursive self-improvement. Anthropic's safety policy treats a doubling of the normal rate of improvement, driven by AI, as the trigger for extra safeguards. The company says none of its current models has crossed that line yet. Sources: TechCrunch, International Business Times Singapore.

item.title: OpenAI is shutting down the old ChatGPT app, and the Work tab is next
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: ChatGPT Classic desktop users now see a banner: the app will retire on January 30, 2027. OpenAI says the full chat history comes along to the new ChatGPT app. OpenAI plans to fold the Work tab into regular ChatGPT, so quick questions and long tasks live in one place. A small group of users will test it first. Codex stays a separate section. In July, OpenAI president Greg Brockman agreed the new desktop app was "kind of a mess." He said that by the end of the year there should be no Work tab. Sources: 9to5Mac, Android Headlines, 9to5Mac (Brockman interview).

Google announced the rename on July 16, 2026, and said the product stays a standalone research tool. Create a notebook","text":"Open Gemini Notebook in your browser and select Create new notebook. In the window that opens, choose Upload a source. Use one notebook per subject or project. Add the right sources","text":"Select Add sources on the left. Gemini Notebook accepts PDFs, Google Docs, Google Slides, Google Sheets, Word, PowerPoint, TXT, Markdown, CSV and ePub files, images, audio files such as MP3 and WAV, pasted text, web links, public YouTube videos and Gemini chats. Gemini Notebook shows results you can import. Turn on Deep Research for a longer search that takes a few minutes; Google says that option is only for users over 18.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ask questions about your own files","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Once sources are in, the chat panel shows a summary of them and suggested questions. Then list the 5 facts I am most likely to be tested on, and point to where each one appears.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Spot the gaps","text":"Compare what [source 1] and [source 2] say about [topic]. List where they agree, where they disagree, and anything one covers that the other leaves out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Click the citations on anything you plan to quote or memorize. The answer is only as good as the passage behind it, and checking takes seconds.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Turn your notes into a podcast","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Audio Overviews live in the Studio panel. Google's help center lists four formats: Deep Dive, the default, where two hosts discuss your sources; The Brief, one speaker giving the key points in under two minutes; The Critique, two hosts giving feedback on something like an essay; and The Debate, two hosts arguing different sides. You can choose Shorter, Default or Longer, though Longer works in English only. More than 80 languages are supported.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Generate an Audio Overview with a focus","text":"In Studio, open Audio Overview, pick a format and length, and add a prompt that says what to focus on and how expert the listener is. It generates in the background, which can take a couple of minutes, so you can keep working. You can download the audio when it is done.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A beginner's audio lesson","text":"Focus only on [chapter or topic]. Explain it for a beginner, use one everyday example per idea, and end with the 3 points I must remember.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is also an Interactive mode. When you create a new Audio Overview with it switched on, you can select Join while listening and ask the hosts a question by voice; they answer from your sources and then carry on. Google says it is English only, works only on newly generated overviews, and may have delays or audio glitches.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Quiz yourself with flashcards and quizzes","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Customize before you generate","text":"In Studio, select Flashcards or Quizzes to generate right away, or click the pencil icon first to customize. You can set the difficulty to easy, medium or hard, choose fewer, standard or more items, and add a prompt about the topic, audience or style.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Questions that test understanding","text":"Make questions only about [topic]. Mix definitions with questions that ask me to apply an idea to a new example. Skip anything not in my sources.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"While you study, the Explain button gives the reasoning behind a card or an answer. On flashcards you mark each card Got it! or Missed it!, and Gemini Notebook saves your progress. At the end you can practice again with the same cards, all cards, or only the ones you missed. Flashcards can be downloaded as a CSV file.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Flashcards or Quizzes","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16958963"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build study guides and reports","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Studio panel also makes notes, Video Overviews, mind maps, data tables, slide decks, infographics and reports. Report types include a study guide, a briefing document, an FAQ or a custom report, and a report can be exported to Google Docs from its three dot menu. Edits you make in the exported Doc do not sync back to the notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A one page study guide","text":"Create a one page study guide on [topic]: key terms with short definitions, a timeline of the main events, and 5 practice questions with answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gemini Notebook is only as good as what you put in. If your sources are thin or wrong, its answers and quizzes will be too, and it will not tell you what your notes are missing unless you ask. Google itself warns that Audio Overviews are AI generated and can contain inaccuracies, so treat them as a way to review, not as the final word. It also cannot combine notebooks, and the mobile app may not support every feature. For a quick fact check against the open web, a search tool is still the better fit; for learning a specific set of material well, this is the tool to use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free accounts get the core features. Google's paid AI plans raise the limits on notebooks, sources and daily generations, and some newer features, such as code that runs inside a notebook to analyze data, started with Google AI Ultra users before a wider rollout.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]}]}

item.title: Microsoft just filed a patent for AI that changes your words live and moves your lips to match
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Microsoft filed a patent application for near real-time AI editing of live video and AR events, patent tracker Patentlyze found. AI agents would remove or replace words, then adjust the speaker's face and mouth to match. Examples include cutting filler words and stutters, and translating a live event into the viewer's language. It could also drop slang like "y'all" or idioms like "bite the bullet", with replacements from internet search. Edits would follow each viewer's profile, so two people could hear different versions of the same live event. Sources: WION, Digit, CXOToday.

Democrats appear likely to win back the House and possibly the Senate, according to TechCrunch, and Axios reported that OpenAI was preparing for a possible blue wave that could bring a more regulation-minded government.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/01/openai-might-rebrand-its-data-centers-as-ai-compute-campuses/"},{"name":"Business Insider","url":"https://sg.news.yahoo.com/openai-wants-everyone-call-ai-222808607.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Other ideas in the plan include developing AI speed limits, showing people how AI helps them in daily life and pushing the United States to help shape global AI standards, TechCrunch reported.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/01/openai-might-rebrand-its-data-centers-as-ai-compute-campuses/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Chris Lehane, OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, told Axios that the midterms will be a preview of the 2028 presidential race, where he expects AI to be a central issue, according to TechCrunch.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/01/openai-might-rebrand-its-data-centers-as-ai-compute-campuses/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why data centers became a campaign issue","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Data centers have become a major issue for voters in this election cycle, Business Insider reported. It cited a recent Pew Research poll in which 54% of Americans said AI data centers are bad for the environment.","sources":[{"name":"Business Insider","url":"https://sg.news.yahoo.com/openai-wants-everyone-call-ai-222808607.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Other large technology companies have tried to win over local communities with money. The outlet noted that the debate has already led Amazon and Microsoft to say they will stop using nondisclosure agreements in negotiations with local governments. Lehane also said communities should hold companies accountable so they receive a real benefit from the projects.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/01/openai-might-rebrand-its-data-centers-as-ai-compute-campuses/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Business Insider noted that it is unclear whether the compute campus name will catch on.","sources":[{"name":"Business Insider","url":"https://sg.news.yahoo.com/openai-wants-everyone-call-ai-222808607.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A new name does not change what these sites need: land, power, water and local approval. item.title: Grok Bot users ran out of usage in days. Elon Musk says it was costing too much
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Grok Bot subscribers said this week that their usage ran out much earlier than expected. One user said usage hit 100% with four days left before the weekly reset. Asked on X on November 1 if usage could be reset, Musk said the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue. He gave no figures and did not say if limits will change. xAI launched Grok Bot in early beta in August. It runs research, writing and browsing tasks on its own virtual computer. Sources: Tesla North, Yeni Safak (Anadolu Agency), explainx.ai.

item.title: 8 AI words everyone is suddenly using, and what they actually mean
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: An agent is an AI that runs its own loop: it picks a tool, checks the result and decides the next step. Anthropic separates agents from workflows, where the steps are fixed in code ahead of time. Sources: Anthropic: Building effective agents, Addy Osmani: Agent harness engineering, Anthropic: Introducing the Model Context Protocol, Anthropic: Equipping agents with Agent Skills, arXiv: GEO, Generative Engine Optimization, Conductor: Answer engine optimization, OpenAI Charter, Wikipedia: Superintelligence.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Eight AI terms explained: agents, harnesses, MCP, skills, GEO, AEO, AGI and superintelligence","dek":"A plain reference to the words behind AI tools, AI search and the long term goals of the largest labs, based on the documents that define them.","summary":"Agents, harnesses, MCP and skills describe how AI models use tools and carry out tasks, while GEO and AEO describe how content gets surfaced in AI answers. AGI and superintelligence name the goals that OpenAI, Meta and others say they are working toward.","seo_title":"AI terms explained: agents, MCP, skills, GEO, AGI and more","seo_description":"What agents, harnesses, MCP, skills, GEO, AEO, AGI and superintelligence mean, explained from the documents that define each term.","answer_summary":"An agent is an AI system that directs its own tool use, a harness is the software around a model, MCP is an open standard for connecting AI to data, and skills are folders of instructions an agent loads when needed. GEO and AEO are about being cited in AI answers, and AGI and superintelligence describe AI that matches or far exceeds human ability.","tags":["AI agents","MCP","Agent Skills","GEO","AGI","Superintelligence"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic described AI agents in a December 19, 2024 research post as systems in which large language models direct their own processes and decide how to use tools. The company said agents are usually language models that call tools in a loop and adjust based on feedback from their environment. It set them apart from workflows, in which a model and its tools follow paths that developers write in code ahead of time.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Building effective agents","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How AI gets things done: harnesses, MCP and skills","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A harness is the layer that turns a model into a working agent. In an April 19, 2026 essay, engineer and author Addy Osmani defined it as all of the code, configuration and execution logic that is not the model itself. That covers system prompts and rule files, tool definitions, the loop that runs the agent, context management, memory files, sandboxes and approval gates. Osmani named Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider and Cline as examples, and wrote that the behavior users see depends heavily on the harness even when the underlying model is the same.","sources":[{"name":"Addy Osmani: Agent harness engineering","url":"https://addyosmani.com/blog/agent-harness-engineering/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Model Context Protocol, or MCP, is an open standard that Anthropic introduced on November 25, 2024 for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data is stored. Developers expose data or tools through an MCP server, and AI applications connect to it as clients. At launch, Anthropic published ready made servers for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres and Puppeteer, and named Block, Apollo, Zed, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph among early adopters.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing the Model Context Protocol","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent Skills, which Anthropic announced on October 16, 2025, are organized folders of instructions, scripts and resources. Each skill is a directory with a SKILL.md file that begins with a short block of metadata, including a name and a description. Claude loads only that name and description at the start, reads the full file when a task calls for the skill, and opens any linked files only if they are needed. Anthropic calls this layered approach progressive disclosure and says it keeps skills from filling the model's context.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Equipping agents with Agent Skills","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The four terms fit together. The model does the reasoning, the harness runs it, MCP connects it to outside apps and data, and skills give it task specific know how without loading everything at once. Osmani argues that much of what separates one coding assistant from another sits in those outer layers rather than in the model alone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How content shows up in AI answers: GEO and AEO","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Generative engine optimization, or GEO, was introduced in a November 2023 paper by researchers from Princeton University and the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. The authors described generative engines as search systems that use AI models to gather and summarize information in answer to a query, and proposed GEO as a way for content creators to improve how visible their content is in those answers. They reported that GEO methods could raise visibility by up to 40 percent in generative engine responses.","sources":[{"name":"arXiv: GEO, Generative Engine Optimization","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Answer engine optimization, or AEO, is a closely related idea. The search marketing company Conductor describes it as structuring content so that AI engines can understand it and use it as a direct answer, in tools such as ChatGPT and Perplexity and in formats such as Google's AI Overviews and featured snippets. Conductor says the goal differs from traditional search engine optimization, which focuses on ranking positions, because AEO aims to be cited as the source of the answer.","sources":[{"name":"Conductor: Answer engine optimization","url":"https://www.conductor.com/academy/glossary/answer-engine-optimization/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where the labs say this is heading: AGI and superintelligence","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's charter defines artificial general intelligence, or AGI, as highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work, and states that the company's mission is to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity. Superintelligence describes a further step. Wikipedia defines it as a hypothetical agent with intelligence beyond the most gifted human minds and cites philosopher Nick Bostrom's definition of an intellect that greatly exceeds human cognitive performance in virtually all domains. Ilya Sutskever's startup Safe Superintelligence focuses only on building a safe superintelligence, and Meta created a division called Meta Superintelligence Labs in 2025.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Charter","url":"https://openai.com/charter/"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Superintelligence","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superintelligence"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The first six terms describe tools and practices that exist today and can be tested. AGI and superintelligence are different: they are goals and definitions for systems that do not exist yet, which makes claims about them harder to check.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch how vendors use these words in product launches. A claim about an agent, a skill or an MCP connector can be checked against the published definitions, while a claim about AGI depends on whose definition is being used.","sources":[]}]}

item.author: NeuraFeed news desk

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Perplexity: how to research with sources you can actually check","dek":"How to ask better questions, choose where Perplexity searches, verify its citations, and use Research mode and Projects for bigger jobs.","summary":"Perplexity searches the web and answers with numbered citations, but the answer is only as good as the question and the sources behind it. Here is how to set up each step, which features need a paid plan, and where Perplexity falls short.","seo_title":"Perplexity Guide: How to Research With Sources","seo_description":"How to use Perplexity for research: narrow questions, the sources menu, checking citations, Research mode and Projects, with copy and paste prompts.","answer_summary":"Ask a specific question, choose the right sources (Web, Academic, Social or Finance), click the numbered citations to check each claim, and select Research in the mode selector when you need a full cited report.","tags":["Perplexity","AI search","Research","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity is an AI search engine. You type a question, it searches the web in real time, and it writes an answer with numbered footnotes that link to the pages it used. That last part is what makes it useful for research: you can check every claim. The catch is that most people read the answer and never open a single source. This guide covers how to ask, how to pick sources, how to check the citations, and when to use Research mode and Projects.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a narrow question","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity handles plain, conversational questions, but specific questions get better answers. Fast Company gives a simple example: a query for the latest breakthroughs in EV battery recycling methods works better than just typing EV batteries. Answers also keep context inside a thread, so you can ask a follow up without repeating the whole question.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Name the topic, the time frame and the output","text":"Say what you want to know, which period it covers, and what shape the answer should take: a list, a comparison, a short summary. If dates matter, ask for the date of each source so you can see how fresh the information is.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: What changed recently","text":"What changed in [topic] between [month, year] and today? Use only sources published in that period, list the 3 most important changes, and give the date of each source.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Keep digging in the same thread","text":"Ask your follow ups as replies in the same thread instead of starting a new search. Perplexity keeps the earlier questions in context, so you can go from a broad overview to one specific detail in a few steps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose where it searches","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The search box has a sources menu that sets where Perplexity looks. Web is the default and covers news, current events and popular sites. Academic leans on scientific papers, scholarly articles and research journals. Social pulls in discussions and firsthand experiences from people, and Finance focuses on market data, company reports and investment news, according to Fast Company.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Switch to Academic for health, science and research questions","text":"When the question is about evidence, not opinion, set the sources to Academic before you search. Then ask Perplexity to separate strong findings from early ones.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: What the studies say","text":"Summarize what peer reviewed studies say about [question]. Separate strong evidence from early or small studies, and say where the studies disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Social when you want real experiences, like how owners feel about a product after a year. Treat those answers as opinions, not facts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Check the citations","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Each answer has numbered citations, and clicking one opens the original page. Dupple's guide warns that the AI can still get things wrong and recommends clicking through to verify claims, especially statistics. Fast Company makes the same point: the citations exist so you can read the summary in its original context.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Ask which source supports which claim","text":"After a long answer, ask Perplexity to map each claim to its source. Then open the sources for the claims you plan to use, and read the sentence yourself. If a number is not on the page, do not use it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Show your work","text":"For each claim in your last answer, tell me which numbered source supports it. Flag any claim that no source directly supports.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Research mode for the big questions","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Research mode is Perplexity's deeper option. According to its help center, it runs many searches, reads a large number of sources and reasons through them to write a full report. You turn it on by selecting Research from the mode selector in the search box, on the web, the mobile apps and the Mac app. Most tasks finish in under 3 minutes, but some take 4 to 5 minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10738684-what-is-research-mode"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free users get limited access to Research mode and Pro subscribers get extended access. Limits reset on a rolling basis, not on a fixed date. You cannot pick the model in Research mode; Perplexity chooses it. When the report is done, you can export it as a PDF or a document, or turn it into a Perplexity Page to share.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10738684-what-is-research-mode"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A full report","text":"Write a research report on [topic] for [who it is for]. Cover [point 1], [point 2] and [point 3], end with a short list of open questions, and cite a source for every number.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For quick everyday questions, the faster standard search is enough. Perplexity describes Pro Search as the deeper option for complex questions: it may ask you follow up questions to refine what you want, and free accounts get a limited number of Pro Searches.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Keep long research in a Project","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Projects are the new name for what Perplexity used to call Spaces; the company renamed them on July 30, 2026, according to Fello AI. A Project keeps searches, files, instructions and connected tools in one place, so you can return to the same research over time.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352961-what-are-projects"},{"name":"Fello AI","url":"https://felloai.com/perplexity-spaces/"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Create a Project","text":"Open the Projects section in the left sidebar and select New project. Give it a title of up to 50 characters. You can add a description, an icon and a color.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Add instructions and files","text":"In the Project settings, add instructions of up to 8,000 characters. They apply to every query you run in that Project, so this is where you put your preferred format or the kinds of sources you trust. Then upload files or whole folders.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The help center lists the same file limits on every plan: up to 10,000 files and 5 GB per Project, with each file up to 100 MB. On personal accounts a Project is visible only to people you give access to, and you can add up to 5 contributors.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352961-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Perplexity falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity is a research shortcut, not a replacement for reading. A summary can flatten a nuance, mix up two sources, or attach a number to the wrong page. The citations make those mistakes easy to catch, but only if you open them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is also not the best tool for every search. Dupple notes that Google is still better for going straight to a specific website or finding a local business. Several features, including more Pro Searches and file uploads, are tied to the paid Pro plan, which both Fast Company and Dupple list at $20 a month.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you share anything Perplexity wrote, open at least the sources behind the numbers. If you cannot find the claim on the page, leave it out.","sources":[]}]}
